title: Block noise phase identity
statement: Let $n,m\in\mathbb N$, $\rho\in\mathbb R$, and $a,b\colon\{1,\ldots,n\}\to\mathbb R$. For a Boolean vector $x$ of length $nm$, divide its coordinates into $n$ blocks of length $m$ and let $z_i(x)$ be the sum of the signs in block $i$, divided by $\sqrt m$. With $\sigma(\mathrm{false})=1$, $\sigma(\mathrm{true})=-1$, and $K_\rho(x,y)=\prod_{r=1}^{nm}\frac{1+\rho\sigma(x_r)\sigma(y_r)}2$, one has $2^{-nm}\sum_{x,y}K_\rho(x,y)\exp\!\bigl(i\sum_i(a_i z_i(x)+b_i z_i(y))\bigr)=\prod_{i=1}^n\left(\frac{1+\rho}{2}\cos\!\left(\frac{a_i+b_i}{\sqrt m}\right)+\frac{1-\rho}{2}\cos\!\left(\frac{a_i-b_i}{\sqrt m}\right)\right)^m$, where both sums range over Boolean vectors of length $nm$.
hypotheses_covered: $a,b$ are real-valued functions on the $n$ coordinates
